title: Record that a release went out
statement: As a developer, I can record that a release went out, and at which commit, so "what shipped" has an answer that a person stated.
overview: Trevor's direction: nothing can block a release. A person decides, and the mark records that they did. It differs from `plan deliver`, which refuses until all is done, partly because a release checklist has steps that only happen afterwards, such as turning something back on.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Only an explicit command marks a release released, and it records when and the commit.
Nothing refuses it: the command lists unchecked steps and stories with no path to code, and proceeds.
Steps can still be checked, and notes corrected, after it is marked.
Reading a released version's stories as they stood uses Git at that commit, and the release stores no copy of them.
